The held Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13886.txt, 84 FR 48041, PDF pages 1-3) carries the heading, the date September 9, 2019 and FR Doc. 2019-19895. The lead terminates the national emergency declared in Executive Order 12947 and revokes that order (as amended by Executive Order 13099) and orders further steps under Executive Order 13224. Section 1 restates section 1 of Executive Order 13224 (blocking of listed persons and of persons determined under criteria, correspondent-account sanctions on foreign financial institutions, and the exception clause); section 2 changes a cross-reference in section 5 of that order; section 3 holds general provisions; section 4 makes the order effective at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on September 10, 2019. The dossier's 19 clauses (with the machine-split paragraphs of section 1(a)(ii) and (iii)) cover the whole text and are accepted. The lead's termination of the Executive Order 12947 emergency and revocation of that order were performed when the order took effect on September 10, 2019, so the lead is terminated by performance; the other 18 clauses are operative. Executive Order 13224 as amended by this order was applied in OFAC designations on October 2, 2026, and the emergency was continued by the notice of September 11, 2026. A search of the held corpus for the number EO 13886 (27 files) finds the order, continuation notices, OFAC notices and rules, 31 CFR part 594 and a 2024 BIS rule; the only revoke-wording is the statement that this order revoked Executive Order 12947. None revokes, supersedes or amends this order. Executive Order 14294 (an unlocated actor in the dossier) is an order on regulatory criminal penalties and does not name it. The held text is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF; page images were not inspected.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"The order states no end date, event or condition; its only effective-time statement (section 4) starts it. The held-corpus search for the number EO 13886 found no revoke, supersede, terminate or rescind wording about this order; the one hit is the statement that this order revoked Executive Order 12947. The OFR catalog, U.S. Code and CFR searches record no disposition. The annual notices of 2020 to 2026 continue the Executive Order 13224 emergency without lapse (the 2019 notice is not held; see the legal basis). The October 2, 2026 OFAC designations apply the amended section 1(a)(iii) and 1(b).\",\"independent_command_check\":\"The independent commands are the termination of the Executive Order 12947 emergency and revocation of that order; the restated blocking command of section 1(a) with its listed-person, determination and carry-over limbs; the correspondent-account authority of 1(b); the exception clause of 1(c); the cross-reference change of section 2; the general provisions of section 3; and the effective time of section 4.\",\"savings_check\":\"Only the lead is terminated; its effects survive as described in the savings reason. The held Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13894.txt, 84 FR 55851, PDF pages 1-5) carries the heading, the date October 14, 2019 and FR Doc. 2019-22849. The dossier's inventory omits the preamble sentence that finds the threat and declares the national emergency and orders ('I hereby declare a national emergency to deal with that threat. I hereby determine and order:'), and splits the paragraphs of section 1(a)(i) and section 2 into machine fragments (including repeated 'dup' scopes), so the inventory is corrected to 25 clauses with exact spans: the lead; section 1(a) with its (i)(A), (i)(B)-(D) and (i)(E)-(F) criteria and 1(b); section 2(a) to (d); section 3(a) to (c); and sections 4 to 12. Two later orders amend the order. Executive Order 14142 (January 15, 2025) strikes a phrase about Turkey from the second paragraph, strikes section 1(a)(i)(B)-(F) and inserts two new criteria (assisting a blocked person; being owned or controlled by or acting for a blocked person), and strikes section 8(f), the definition of Government of Turkey. Executive Order 14312 (June 30, 2025) expands the scope of the emergency and strikes and restates section 1(a) and section 2(a). Under the owner ruling on strike-and-insert amendments, clauses so amended continue, amended, with the amendment recorded as a later event; a clause struck without replacement ends on the date of the striking order. On that basis the Turkey-related criteria in section 1(a)(i)(B)-(D) and the definition in section 8(f) are terminated by Executive Order 14142 on 2025-01-15; the other clauses are operative on 2026-10-14. The emergency was continued by the notice of September 30, 2026. A search of the held corpus for the number EO 13894 (32 files) finds the order, Executive Orders 14142 and 14312, the annual notices, State and Treasury notices and rules and 31 CFR part 569; the only wording that ends anything is the 2025 amendments. The held text is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF; page images were not inspected. The substance of section 1(a) and section 2(a) changed in 2025 and the later events mark that for the reviewer.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"The order states no end date, event or condition. The held annual continuation notices of 2020 to 2026 continue the emergency; none terminates it. The held-corpus number search found two ending events, both amendments by later presidential orders: Executive Order 14142 (2025-01-15), whose strikings end the clauses listed above, and Executive Order 14312 (2025-06-30), which restates sections 1(a) and 2(a) without ending them. Earlier events do not end the Turkey-related clauses: the Treasury notice of 2020 unblocking named Turkish officials removes persons from the list (individual delistings) and is not an act of the President striking the criteria. The Department of State notices of 2020 designate persons and end nothing. The OFR catalog, U.S. Code and CFR searches record no revocation of the order.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"The independent commands are the declaration of emergency; the blocking command and its criteria groups; the exception clauses in 1(b), 2(d) and 3(c); the sanctions authority in section 2(a) and the procurement/visa and financial sanctions of 2(b) and 2(c); the foreign-financial-institution authority of section 3; the entry suspension of section 4; the donations determination of section 5; the inclusion rules of section 6; the evasion and conspiracy prohibitions of section 7; the definitions of section 8 (with 8(f) separate); the no-prior-notice determination of section 9; the delegation of section 10; the report authority of section 11; and the general provisions of section 12.\",\"savings_check\":\"Two clauses (section 1(a)(i)(B)-(D) and section 8(f)) are terminated; the savings reason states what survives. The other clauses continue, amended where a later event is recorded.\",\"scope_check\":\"Clauses are decided separately: the Turkey-related criteria (section 1(a)(i)(B)-(D)) and the definition of Government of Turkey (section 8(f)) were struck by Executive Order 14142 without replacement; the assistance and ownership criteria (section 1(a)(i)(E)-(F)) were replaced by new criteria (B) and (C) Order 13894 of October 14, 2019 (84 FR 55851), Blocking Property and Suspending Entry of Certain Persons Contributing to the Situation in Syria, declares a national emergency and has twelve sections. The held Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13894.txt, 84 FR 55851, PDF pages 1-5) carries the heading, the date October 14, 2019 and FR Doc. 2019-22849. The dossier's inventory omits the preamble sentence that finds the threat and declares the national emergency and orders ('I hereby declare a national emergency to deal with that threat. I hereby determine and order:'), and splits the paragraphs of section 1(a)(i) and section 2 into machine fragments (including repeated 'dup' scopes), so the inventory is corrected to 25 clauses with exact spans: the lead; section 1(a) with its (i)(A), (i)(B)-(D) and (i)(E)-(F) criteria and 1(b); section 2(a) to (d); section 3(a) to (c); and sections 4 to 12. Two later orders amend the order. Executive Order 14142 (January 15, 2025) strikes a phrase about Turkey from the second paragraph, strikes section 1(a)(i)(B)-(F) and inserts two new criteria (assisting a blocked person; being owned or controlled by or acting for a blocked person), and strikes section 8(f), the definition of Government of Turkey. Executive Order 14312 (June 30, 2025) expands the scope of the emergency and strikes and restates section 1(a) and section 2(a). Under the owner ruling on strike-and-insert amendments, clauses so amended continue, amended, with the amendment recorded as a later event; a clause struck without replacement ends on the date of the striking order. On that basis the Turkey-related criteria in section 1(a)(i)(B)-(D) and the definition in section 8(f) are terminated by Executive Order 14142 on 2025-01-15; the other clauses are operative on 2026-10-14. The emergency was continued by the notice of September 30, 2026. A search of the held corpus for the number EO 13894 (32 files) finds the order, Executive Orders 14142 and 14312, the annual notices, State and Treasury notices and rules and 31 CFR part 569; the only wording that ends anything is the 2025 amendments. The held text is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF; page images were not inspected. The substance of section 1(a) and section 2(a) changed in 2025 and the later events mark that for the reviewer.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"The order states no end date, event or condition. The held annual continuation notices of 2020 to 2026 continue the emergency; none terminates it. The held-corpus number search found two ending events, both amendments by later presidential orders: Executive Order 14142 (2025-01-15), whose strikings end the clauses listed above, and Executive Order 14312 (2025-06-30), which restates sections 1(a) and 2(a) without ending them. Earlier events do not end the Turkey-related clauses: the Treasury notice of 2020 unblocking named Turkish officials removes persons from the list (individual delistings) and is not an act of the President striking the criteria. The Department of State notices of 2020 designate persons and end nothing. The OFR catalog, U.S. Code and CFR searches record no revocation of the order.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"The independent commands are the declaration of emergency; the blocking command and its criteria groups; the exception clauses in 1(b), 2(d) and 3(c); the sanctions authority in section 2(a) and the procurement/visa and financial sanctions of 2(b) and 2(c); the foreign-financial-institution authority of section 3; the entry suspension of section 4; the donations determination of section 5; the inclusion rules of section 6; the evasion and conspiracy prohibitions of section 7; the definitions of section 8 (with 8(f) separate); the no-prior-notice determination of section 9; the delegation of section 10; the report authority of section 11; and the general provisions of section 12.\",\"savings_check\":\"Two clauses (section 1(a)(i)(B)-(D) and section 8(f)) are terminated; the savings reason states what survives. The other clauses continue, amended where a later event is recorded.\",\"scope_check\":\"Clauses are decided separately: the Turkey-related criteria (section 1(a)(i)(B)-(D)) and the definition of Government of Turkey (section 8(f)) were struck by Executive Order 14142 without replacement; the assistance and ownership criteria (section 1(a)(i)(E)-(F)) were replaced by new criteria (B) and (C) with the same content; section 1(a) and section 2(a) were restated by Executive Order 14312; the remaining clauses are -held/applied-v8/CLAIMS.proposed.jsonl","pointer":"line:8"}],"reported_material_gaps":[],"research_rationale":"Executive Order 13915 of April 14, 2020 (85 FR 21733), Providing an Order of Succession Within the Department of the Interior, is a four-section order. The held Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13915.txt, 85 FR 21733, PDF pages 1-2) carries the heading, the date April 14, 2020 and the FR Doc. 2020-08392 line, so the identity matches the register row. Section 1 makes the officers named in section 2 act as Secretary of the Interior, subject to section 3, when both the Secretary and the Deputy Secretary of the Interior have died, resigned or are otherwise unable to perform the duties. Section 2 lists seven officers in order. Section 3(a) provides that no officer serving in a listed office in an acting capacity acts as Secretary by virtue of that service, and section 3(b) keeps the President's discretion, to the extent the Vacancies Reform Act permits, to designate an acting Secretary differently. Section 4 revokes Executive Order 13244 of December 18, 2001, and that command was executed when the order was signed on April 14, 2020. The order states no expiry date, event or condition. Its commands are conditional (they apply only when the offices of Secretary and Deputy Secretary are both unavailable), but a condition that has not occurred does not end a command. A search of the held corpus for the number EO 13915 finds only the order's own Federal Register page and the Federal Register copy of FR Doc. 2020-08392; no later order, notice or regulation held cites it, and the three bounded searches report no hit that amends, revokes or supersedes it. The status on 2026-10-14 is operative for the section 1 to 3 commands and the enacting lead, and terminated by performance on 2020-04-14 for section 4. The authority statute's text is not held; this is disclosed in the legal basis, and nothing held shows that the statute was repealed or expired.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"The order states no end date, event or condition. Its only dated statements are the signing date April 14, 2020 and the Federal Register filing line, neither of which ends anything. A search of the held corpus for the number EO 13915 (jobs/*/output/texts, excluding clause drafts) finds only the order's own Federal Register page and the Federal Register copy of FR Doc. 2020-08392, so no later order, notice or regulation that revokes, supersedes or amends it is held. The OFR catalog search records no disposition note, the eCFR/CFR search found no regulation naming the order, and the only U.S. Code lead is a 2025-01-06 Table IV listing line. The section 3 exceptions and the conditional wording of section 1 limit when an officer acts; they do not end a command.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"The independent commands are: the enacting lead citing the Vacancies Reform Act; the section 1 command that listed officers act as Secretary when both the Secretary and Deputy Secretary are unavailable; the section 2 list of seven offices in order (each lettered paragraph is decided separately); section 3(a) excluding officers serving in an acting capacity; section 3(b) preserving presidential discretion to depart from the list; and the section 4 revocation of Executive Order 13244. Sections 2 and 3 are dependent on section 1's trigger but are separate propositions.\",\"savings_check\":\"Only section 4 is terminated. Its effect, the revocation of Executive Order 13244, was complete when it was signed and survives as the continuing absence of that order; no pending proceeding or accrued right depends on it. Sections 1 to 3 continue, so there is nothing to transfer.\",\"scope_check\":\"No later instrument touches any section. Section 4 revoked a different order (Executive Order 13244), and a revocation of that order does not reach this one.
